weather.tip: 100% rain chance holding into the evening — keep an umbrella handy for your commute home and budget extra time for waterlogged stretches.

around.headline: Heavy vehicles to be barred from entering Bengaluru during peak hours from next month
around.summary: The city is set to prohibit heavy vehicles from entering during peak traffic hours starting next month, per Public TV English. If you run deliveries or drive a commercial vehicle, plan routes and timings around the new restriction once it's notified.

around.headline: Metro update: Blue Line airport line hits 72% work; Pink Line still awaiting CMRS nod
around.summary: The 58-km Blue Line to the airport is 72% complete with a phased opening planned, while the Pink Line has cleared a Railway Board hurdle but still needs CMRS safety clearance before it can open, per The Times of India and The Hindu. Don't bank on either line for your commute just yet — both dates have slipped before.
around.source: The Times of India, The Hindu

around.headline: Faulty traffic signals leaving traffic police exposed to health hazards
around.summary: Malfunctioning traffic signals at several junctions are forcing traffic police to manually manage flow for longer stretches, exposing them to heat and pollution, per The Hindu. Expect less predictable signal timing at affected junctions — watch the road, not just the light.

around.headline: Four from Pune killed as SUV crashes on Chennai-Bengaluru expressway
around.summary: Four people travelling from Pune died after their SUV hit a divider on the Chennai-Bengaluru expressway, per The Times of India and Deccan Herald. A reminder to slow down on unfamiliar high-speed stretches, especially after dark.
around.source: The Times of India, Deccan Herald

around.headline: KPSC job scam: court denies bail to IAS officer Gyanendra Gangwar
around.summary: A Bengaluru court refused bail to IAS officer Gyanendra Gangwar in the KPSC recruitment scam case, despite a plea citing cancer treatment, per The Times of India. The case remains a reminder to verify any government-job offer directly with KPSC rather than through middlemen.

around.headline: Gold rates ticking up again today
around.summary: Gold prices moved higher across major cities including Bengaluru today, per BusinessLine. If you're planning a festive-season purchase, it's worth comparing today's rate against a few days' trend before buying.

around.headline: Supreme Court plea seeks CEC's prosecution, SIT probe into SIR voter-roll deletions
around.summary: A plea in the Supreme Court has sought prosecution of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and an SIT inquiry into voter deletions during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision, per Live Law — the same exercise that flagged disproportionate deletions across several Bengaluru assembly seats earlier this month. If you haven't checked your name on the draft roll yet, do it before the correction window shuts.

events.name: Six acts, one 24-hour music fest
events.note: A day-long, six-act music festival runs for 24 hours straight in the city, per Deccan Herald.

events.name: Blue & Behold: Cyanotype Exhibition
events.note: A World Cyanotype Day exhibition brings together 50 homegrown artists working in the blue-toned photographic technique, per The New Indian Express and homegrown.co.in.

events.name: Viva La Vino wine-tasting festival
events.note: Sommeliers host an approachable, unpretentious wine-tasting festival for the city, per The Hindu.

events.name: Hiriyara Jaatre — fair for elders
events.note: An annual fair dedicated to senior citizens returns to the city, per Deccan Herald.

street_smart.title: You needed cash urgently last month and took a quick loan through an app you found via an online ad — approved in minutes, no paperwork. Signing up, you allowed it full access to your contacts and photo gallery to speed things along. Your payment is four days late, and today a caller says: pay a ₹5,000 'penalty' right now, or a morphed photo of you goes out to your entire contact list within the hour. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Evergreen rotation (loan-app harassment) — this mechanism last ran as a street-smart topic on 2026-09-01, over three weeks ago (the 2026-09-05 scenario was in-person violence by informal-lender recovery agents, a distinct mechanism). No incident in today's feeds gave a choice-based trap with enough detail to anchor a fresh scenario.
street_smart.situation: The app isn't one you recognize from any bank or NBFC ad — you found it through a Google search result promising instant approval with no credit check.

choices.text: Pay the ₹5,000 'penalty' immediately over the phone to make the threat go away.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Paying doesn't end it — it confirms the threat works, and the same caller (or the next one) will come back with a bigger demand. The 'penalty' has no legal basis to begin with.

choices.text: Refuse the extra payment, screenshot the threats, report the app and caller to the National Cyber Crime helpline (1930) or cybercrime.gov.in, and give a few close contacts a heads-up that a fake, morphed image may circulate.
choices.feedback: Correct. RBI's digital-lending rules cap what can legally be recovered to the principal and disclosed interest, and explicitly ban contacting a borrower's contacts to pressure repayment — so this is a reportable crime, not a debt dispute. Warning your contacts in advance also strips the blackmail of its power, since they'll know to ignore or report the image rather than be shocked by it.

choices.text: Uninstall the app and block the number, and leave it at that.
choices.feedback: Risky. Blocking stops new calls, but the app already has your contacts and photos — without a report, there's nothing stopping them from following through on the threat or targeting someone else the same way.

choices.text: Try to negotiate the caller down to a smaller 'settlement' amount to close the matter quietly.
choices.feedback: Risky. Negotiating treats an extortion demand as a legitimate debt with enforceable terms — it isn't. Agreeing to any amount just confirms you're willing to pay under pressure.

takeaways: Before installing any lending app, check whether it's run by an RBI-registered NBFC or bank partner (listed on the RBI website) — most harassment-based instant-loan apps aren't.
Only the principal plus disclosed, RBI-capped interest and fees are legally recoverable; a phone threat demanding an extra 'penalty' to avoid harassment has no legal standing.

Report contact-list harassment or morphed-image threats immediately to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in — RBI's 2023 digital lending guidelines specifically prohibit lenders from contacting a borrower's personal contacts to pressure repayment.

quiz.question: Starting next month, what will be barred from entering Bengaluru during peak traffic hours?
quiz.why: Restricting heavy/commercial vehicle movement to off-peak hours is a common tactic cities use to ease congestion on arterial roads without limiting everyday commuter traffic.

quiz.question: As of today's report, how much of the Blue Line (Bengaluru's airport metro) construction is complete?
quiz.why: The 58-km Blue Line, connecting the city to Kempegowda International Airport, is planned to open in phases rather than all at once.

quiz.question: An IAS officer was denied bail today in connection with what kind of scam?
options: A KPSC (Karnataka Public Service Commission) recruitment scam
quiz.why: KPSC conducts recruitment exams for a wide range of Karnataka state government posts, so a scam involving it can affect thousands of genuine job aspirants who sat for the same exams.

quiz.question: The Cauvery river, a long-running source of water-sharing dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, originates in which Karnataka district?
quiz.why: The Cauvery rises at Talakaveri in Kodagu, and its inter-state sharing has been governed by tribunal awards and Supreme Court rulings for over a century.

quiz.question: What term describes a sustained rise in the general price level of goods and services in an economy?
quiz.why: India's central bank, the RBI, follows a formal inflation-targeting framework, aiming to keep retail inflation around 4%, with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2 percentage points.
